To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have implemented a set of physics processes for microdosimetric simulations in Geant4, that we have validated these processes against published experimental data and that the processes have been released to the public in a first Geant4 version.
we developed a set of physics models for Geant4 that can be used for microdosimetric calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a set of physical processes specific for simulation of radiation effects at the cellular level.
the design and implementation of new physical processes for Geant4 simulation of radiation interactions with water at low energies.
the design and implementation of new physical processes for Geant4 simulation of microdosimetric quantities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this is an excellent and timely contribution to the field of radiation dosimetry, which is of particular importance in view of the current interest in the development of new radiotherapy modalities, such as proton and carbon ion therapy, where the microdosimetric quantities are of particular importance.
Geant4 is the most versatile and powerful simulation tool currently available for microdosimetric studies.
this work represents a major step towards the implementation of the first Geant4 microdosimetry package.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully implemented a set of physics models that are specific for microdosimeter simulation, and that we have designed a framework for handling particle interactions at the lowest energy scales, with the possibility for adding new models in the future.

we have developed a set of models for Geant4 that are specifically designed for the simulation of the interaction of electrons, proton and light ions in water and other materials of biological relevance.
the new physics models are based on a solid foundation and are ready for use in microdosimetry simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Geant4 is a suitable platform for microdosimetric simulations, provided the physics domain of interest is covered with appropriate models.
a new design is needed to efficiently handle the physics processes relevant for microdosimetric simulation.
a careful selection of physical processes is necessary in order to achieve a reasonable balance of computational efficiency and accuracy, especially for the case of low-energy particles.
